Eligibility criteria (text) items 3-4: "Manual Muscle Testing-8 (MMT-8) score <142, with at least 2 other abnormal Core Set Measures (CSM) (Visual Analogue Scale [VAS] of patient global activity >=2 cm, physician's global disease activity >=2 cm, extra-muscular activity >=2 cm; at least one muscle enzyme >1.5 times upper limit of normal, Health Assessment Questionnaire >=0.25)." MMT-8 <142 was a required threshold; the remaining criteria (physician global VAS, HAQ-DI, patient global VAS, extra-muscular activity VAS, muscle enzyme elevation) formed an "at least 2 of 5 abnormal" requirement, not all independently mandatory -- this atlas's SCORE_CRITERION shape has no "any N of M" operator, so 2 representative CSM thresholds (physician global VAS, HAQ-DI) are recorded here as illustrative members of that 5-item set, not as independently-required criteria; the full 5-item CSM list and its 2016 ACR/EULAR Total Improvement Score composition is in molecule/endpoints source_excerpt fields. Diagnosis itself required the 2017 EULAR/ACR (VALOR-era language) / Bohan and Peter (ProDERM's own protocol language) classification criteria for definite or probable dermatomyositis -- a categorical diagnostic rule, not a numeric score, so not represented as a ScoreCriterion row.

ProDERM statistical methods (PMC7793357): single primary endpoint (TIS >=20 at Week 16) tested at a two-sided alpha=0.05 via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test comparing responder proportions (Octagam vs. placebo) -- no multiple-primary-endpoint gatekeeping procedure (unlike the AD trials' co-primary IGA+EASI-75 hierarchy); secondary endpoints were analyzed descriptively/via ANCOVA and Kaplan-Meier without formal Type-I-error allocation. Sample size: 94 evaluable patients planned for 80% power. Missing data: not imputed except last-observation-carried-forward for the Week-16 ANCOVA when values were missing due to early termination or treatment switch. Both intention-to-treat and per-protocol analysis sets were used.

ProDERM design (PMC7793357 + CT.gov resultsSection): First Period visits/infusions at Weeks 0, 4, 8, 12 with response assessment at Week 16 (primary endpoint); Core Set Measures and CDASI assessed at each visit plus Weeks 28 and 40; SF-36v2 at baseline, Week 16, and Week 40. Extension Period: 6-month open-label Octagam 10% with infusions every 4 weeks (last cycle starting Week 36) through a Week 40 final assessment, with an investigator-discretion dose reduction from 2.0 to 1.0 g/kg available from Week 28 onward for stable/improving subjects. Total trial duration 40 weeks; each infusion cycle comprised infusions given over 2-5 consecutive days.

source_excerpt: ProDERM deterioration/escape rules (PMC7793357): "Deterioration was considered confirmed if worsening was observed on 2 consecutive visits," defined as worsening of >=2 cm in Physician's Global Disease Activity (10 cm VAS) AND >=20% worsening in MMT-8; OR >=2 cm global extra-muscular activity worsening; OR >=30% worsening in any 3 of 5 Core Set Measures. At Week 8 or later, confirmed deterioration triggered a blinded switch to the other treatment arm; subjects on Octagam who confirmed deterioration between Week 8-16 were discontinued at the end of the First Period. Switched/rescued subjects were counted as non-responders on the primary Week-16 TIS analysis. This schema's RESCUE shape (topical-then-systemic step-up, as used for the AD trials) does not fit a blinded-crossover escape design; fields describing topical/systemic step-up are left null and the actual switch mechanism is recorded in `rationale` and `trigger_rules`/`flare_definition` as the closest structural fit.

source_excerpt: 8.1.4. Multiple Comparisons/Multiplicity: Hierarchical testing will be used to control for multiple comparisons (Figure 1). For the primary efficacy analysis and the key secondary efficacy analyses, a <=0.025 (two-sided) alpha-level will be allocated to each dose for comparison with placebo to adjust for multiplicity of testing associated with two doses. Once p>0.025 is observed for a treatment group comparison, inference for additional endpoints is no longer alpha-level protected for that dose group, however nominal p-values will still be reported. Subsequently, conditional upon significance (<=0.025) for the primary endpoint and first key secondary endpoint for each dose, a linear hierarchical testing approach with <=0.025 (two-sided) alpha-level will be used to test the remaining key secondary endpoint comparisons versus placebo.
